name: mathematical-symbols

description.en: 45 common mathematical symbols and what they mean: logic (∀, ∃, ¬, ∧, ∨, ⇒, ⇔), sets and number sets (∈, ⊆, ⊂, ∪, ∩, ℕ, ℝ …), relations (≠, ≈, ∝, ≤, ≡ …), operators (∑, ∏, √, ∫, ∂, ∇, n! …) and the constants π, e and i, plus ∞. Front: the symbol, in a short expression where it needs one (⌊x⌋, g ∘ f); back: its meaning in English and Swedish. ⊂ is read as proper subset and ℕ includes 0. Checked against Wikidata, the Unicode Character Database and the English and Swedish Wikipedia.

Kontrollerade mot Wikidata, Unicodes teckendatabas och engelskspråkiga och svenskspråkiga Wikipedia.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (the Unicode Character Database, live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

Candidate symbols: the library editor's brief named about 45 symbols in five groups (logic, sets, relations, operators, constants). For each, Wikidata was searched for the items that carry the symbol as Unicode character (P487) (query 1) and the statements of those items (query 2), which link character items to concepts through notation (P913), depicts (P180), has use (P366) or symbolizes (P4878).

ISO 80000-2 as recorded in Wikidata: query 3 listed every Wikidata item described by ISO 80000-2:2019 (Q109490582) with the item number (P958 section, e.g. "2-6.8") and the standard's verbal equivalent (P1810 subject named as, e.g. "B is properly included in A"). Every card's concept was matched to one of these records where one exists (all but ∝, and ∫ via the indefinite integral item); this is what the evidence calls the ISO item number. The standard's own tables could not be read: the ISO Online Browsing Platform answered 403 (https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/en/#iso:std:iso:80000:-2:ed-2:v1:en), and the publisher's free preview (query 10) ends after clause 4. From the preview only clause 4's sentence on mathematical constants (e, π, i) is used.

Concepts and labels: query 4 fetched, for the chosen concept items, the English and Swedish labels, Swedish aliases, P487, the notation items with their characters and the ISO records; query 5 the Swedish Wikipedia article title and the character items linked to each concept; query 6 the P487, P913 and P1343 statements that the build checks. While doing so the Query Service was found to return "ℜ" (U+211C) as P487 of the set of real numbers (Q1174982) where the Wikidata API returns "ℝ" (U+211D) (queries 7 and 8); see round 0.

Characters: UnicodeData.txt of the Unicode Character Database 18.0.0 was downloaded (query 11) and the script ucd.py (query 12) printed the line of every character used on a front, which fixed the exact code point (for example U+2223 DIVIDES rather than U+007C VERTICAL LINE for "a ∣ b", U+2216 SET MINUS rather than the backslash for "A ∖ B") and gave the official character name as a check of the meaning.

Independent check in English: the wikitext of the English Wikipedia "Glossary of mathematical symbols" (query 11) was searched with grep_en.py (query 13) and grep (query 14) for the entry of each symbol; each card's meaning agrees with it (∠, π, e and i are not in the glossary). The English Wikipedia article "Natural number" (query 15) was read for the ISO convention on 0.

Swedish: the Swedish Wikipedia "Lista över matematiska symboler" (query 11, wikitext extracted by query 20) and Swedish Wikipedia articles on the concepts (svwiki.py, query 16: 46 titles tried, 41 found, two of them redirects to the same article; plain-text extracts with revision ids; grep_sv.py, query 17; in round 3 also "Skilt från-tecknet", query 24) were read to confirm the Swedish terms. The Swedish backs are standard Swedish terminology chosen by the compiler: single words or set phrases, not protected expression. Where Wikidata has the term as an sv label or alias, the back follows it (konjunktion, disjunktion, negation, implikation, delmängd, union, snitt, tomma mängden, mindre/större än eller lika med, summa, produkt, kvadratrot, absolutbelopp, golvfunktion, takfunktion, fakultet, sammansatt funktion, nablaoperatorn, imaginära enheten, oändlighet, vinkel, Eulers tal, "inte lika med-tecknet" for ≠); the other readings (för alla, det finns, implicerar, om och endast om, är ett element i, äkta delmängd, mängddifferens, kongruent modulo n, delar, proportionell mot, ungefär lika med, plus eller minus) are the usual ones, which the Swedish list and articles only confirmed; no sentences, notes or selection were taken from them. Swedish lower-case style is used throughout (Wikidata's "Partiell derivata" is written "partiell derivata"), named sets and constants with an adjective take the Swedish double definite form ("de naturliga talen", "den tomma mängden", "den imaginära enheten"), and Swedish decimal commas are used in the Swedish notes.

Writing the cards: the backs are the compiler's own short wording of the meaning, in the form in which the symbol is read ("is an element of", "för alla"), with the concept name in brackets where the reading alone is a bare word ("and (conjunction)"). Fronts are text in no language (zxx). A symbol is shown in a short expression where it has another common meaning or could be mistaken for another character: "A ∖ B", "a ≡ b (mod n)", "a ∣ b", "|x|", "⌊x⌋", "⌈x⌉", "n!", "g ∘ f". The constants π, e and i have the front note "a mathematical constant" so that e and i are not read as variables (or e as the elementary charge). Notes give a formula, an example or the convention used, in the compiler's own words and with examples of the compiler's own choosing; examples are introduced with "for example" / "till exempel", and notes that are sentences end with a full stop. Expression fronts get expression readings ("absolute value of x", "floor of x", "g composed with f").

Checks: every card has Wikidata checks run by the builder against live Wikidata: the symbol (P487 on the concept or on its character item), the link between character and concept (P913, P180 or P366), a stable label in English or Swedish, and the concept's ISO 80000-2 record (P1343 Q109490582). Checks were left out where Wikidata disagrees with the card or the Query Service returns a different character (⊂ on subset, ℝ, e); see round 0.

Left out: ⊥ (U+22A5 UP TACK is also the logical constant false, and Unicode has a separate U+27C2 PERPENDICULAR, so the front would be ambiguous between characters and meanings); ≪ and ≫ (no Swedish source for the reading was found beyond the plain translation; the Swedish Wikipedia search for "mycket mindre än", query 22, gave 186 hits, the first ten all outside mathematics); ∄, ∃!, ∴, ∵ and ∮ (not in the brief and outside ISO 80000-2's tables as recorded in Wikidata); ≡ alone (identity, congruence or logical equivalence) and the bare vertical bar (absolute value, divides, such that), which appear only in expressions that fix one meaning.
selection: 45 symbols in five groups, chosen from the library editor's brief and grouped broadly as ISO 80000-2:2019's clauses (as recorded in Wikidata): logic ∀ ∃ ¬ ∧ ∨ ⇒ ⇔ (7); sets ∈ ∉ ∅ ⊆ ⊂ ∪ ∩ ∖ and the number sets ℕ ℤ ℚ ℝ ℂ (13); relations and geometry ≠ ≈ ∝ ≤ ≥, congruence modulo n, divides, parallel and angle (9); operators ∑ ∏ √ ± |x| ⌊x⌋ ⌈x⌉ n! ∘ ∫ ∂ ∇ (12); the constants π, e and i and the symbol ∞ (4). Each is a symbol a student meets in upper-secondary or first-year university mathematics and has one standard meaning given the front. Where usage differs the card states the convention in its note: ⊂ is a proper subset (with ⊆ for subset), as in the Swedish Wikipedia list and the reading that pairs ⊂ with ⊆, and ℕ includes 0, as in ISO 80000-2 and Skolverket's terminology. Left out: ⊥ (two characters, and also "false"), ≪ and ≫, ∄, ∃!, ∴, ∵, ∮, and symbols whose meaning depends on context without a disambiguating expression (≡ alone, |, ~, ×, Δ, →).

"""Fetch the plain-text content and revision id of Swedish Wikipedia articles (verification of Swedish terms).
Usage: python3 svwiki.py   -> writes svwiki-articles.json"""
import json, urllib.parse, urllib.request, pathlib

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).parent
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
TITLES = ["Delmängd", "Kongruens (talteori)", "Moduloräkning", "Delbarhet", "Proportionalitet (matematik)", "E (tal)",
          "Imaginära enheten", "Golv- och takfunktionerna", "Heltalsdel", "Sammansatt funktion", "Partiell derivata",
          "Nablaoperatorn", "Parallell (matematik)", "Vinkel", "Olikhet", "Likhetstecken", "Naturliga tal",
          "Mängddifferens", "Differens (mängdlära)", "Element (mängdlära)", "Absolutbelopp", "Fakultet (matematik)",
          "Allkvantifikator", "Existenskvantifikator", "Implikation", "Ekvivalens (logik)", "Konjunktion (logik)",
          "Disjunktion", "Negation", "Union (matematik)", "Snitt", "Tomma mängden", "Oändlighet", "Pi", "Integral",
          "Summa", "Produkt (matematik)", "Kvadratrot", "Plus–minustecken", "Heltal", "Rationella tal", "Reella tal",
          "Komplexa tal", "Ungefär lika med", "Skilt från-tecken", "Mycket mindre än"]

findings.issue: The Swedish Wikipedia evidence quoted only the article's first sentence ("Golv- och takfunktionerna är två funktioner inom talteorin."), which neither defines ⌈x⌉ nor names takfunktionen.
findings.resolution: Confirmed against the wikitext of revision 55013587 (fetched again 2026-10-04): the article says "'''Takfunktionen''' <math>\lceil x \rceil</math> ger på motsvarande sätt det minsta heltal som är större än eller lika med ''x''." The evidence now quotes that sentence. The same reading showed that the note's first example, ⌈2,1⌉ = 3, is also the article's first ceiling example, although round 3 described the examples as new; it was changed to ⌈3.2⌉ = 4 / ⌈3,2⌉ = 4 so that no example coincides with the article's.

findings.issue: The first method paragraph named only live Wikidata and the validators as machine checks, although every front character was checked against UnicodeData.txt (queries 11 and 12) and with Python unicodedata in round 1.
findings.resolution: Confirmed. The deck-specific slot now reads "(the Unicode Character Database, live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators)".
